title: The operation names of the five consumed rows are not published
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2, T5.1, T5.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.7.2 integration points); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP table, R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3 and 7; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9 Call-type summary; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.1; s12.2; s12.8
description: The route-scoring step consumes five rows across four owners and no source document publishes the operation name of any of them: the rwb-source-data data product that carries the score of v_ace_score and the return per route, the route-agent call of rwb-agent, the rule-in-force and decision-log read of rwb-decision, and the authorise operation of rwb-access, plus the case-state read of rwb-case which TSD names only as a family. The FSD names the integration point as 'Workbench, Model gateway' and gives no operation; TSD S1 T5.1 declares no external interface and T5.2 describes the calls as published Java interfaces of the monolith. The baseline and the application story therefore build against a documented use and a placeholder, and no path, parameter, model code or transport is invented.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 three REST operations and name no consumed operation; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 only; TSD S1 T5.1 is the row 'None'; FSD S1 A2.7.2 names the integration points as 'Workbench, Model gateway' and gives no operation; the legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E4-007 lists POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/route only.
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data owner, P10 rwb-agent owner, P3 rwb-case owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: The five owners publish their operation names before the wave 3 tag; the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use in the meantime, and a published name replaces the placeholder in a minor contract version with no behaviour change.

title: The recommendation element set, the reasons and the alternatives are not published, and the route operation already carries the appraisal slice
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.7.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-007 Endpoints, AC1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S1 rwb-valuation (Valuation and route)/RWB S1 E4001 CON Order an appraisal when the last one is stale - contract v1.md (s12.1)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 9; s12.1 REST operations provided; CON s1; s2; s3; s12.1
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be written with the rule version and AC1 requires the recommendation to state the reasons and the alternatives, but no source publishes the element set of that answer: TSD S1 T-A.2 declares RouteRequest in and Approval out and names no element, and the legacy Data table carries the decision record and the score rows only. At the same time POST /cases/{caseId}/route on the service base is already baselined with the appraisal and approval elements by RWB-S1-E4001-CON, so two baselines of one service touch one operation while the lane rule gives one owner per operation. The baseline declares the recommendation, its reasons, its alternatives, the confidence and the versions as an additive minor slice of the operation that exists and declares no second path, and the window from v_ace_score is read on the data product rather than added as a table.
evidence: TSD S1 T-A.2 gives Request RouteRequest, Response Approval and no element; the FSD S1 A2.7.2 functional overview names the recommendation, the reasons and the alternatives and gives no element; the legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E4-007 lists one path; RWB-S1-E4001-CON s12.1 declares the same path with the appraisal, order and interface-run elements.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the owner of RWB-S1-E4001-CON
proposed: The service owner confirms the recommendation element list at the tag and the two baselines are published as one document family, this one as a minor version; if the elements belong to a separate operation the owner names it before the wave 3 tag.

title: No S1 route-decision rule package is in force and no source names the decision code, the confidence threshold or the open route set as data
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.7.3.1 BR-S1-007, A2.7.4.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-37 to R-UNI-41, R-RES-32); _work/msr/extract/B-AI-31/Recovery Workbench Agent Catalog and Specifications v2.md (Route agent, D6.3); Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3 (NFR-055)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2, 5 and 8; s8 BR2, BR5; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data; CON s3, s8, s12
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be written with the rule version, and no rule id is in force for this step: the routing logic carries no S1 row for scoring or recommending a route, D6.3 is an agent sub-decision and not a rule row, and the S1 package is Phase 2 in the detailed design. No source names the confidence threshold, the ranking weights, the reasons vocabulary or the open route set as a reference-data row either, and the only published rule that changes the set is R-RES-32, which excludes R1 after a second break. The story reads whatever is in force with its version, records that version, applies the allowed-action check and the confidence threshold as data and writes no threshold, weight or route code in code.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.7.3.1 gives BR-S1-007, that no value a business person may change is written in code and is read from reference data with its version; A2.7.4.1 states the result is recorded with its rule version; the Rules sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 carries no S1 row for a route score or recommendation; TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-ROUTE only; the Agent Catalog gives D6.3 as an agent step with L1 at go-live and L2 target; NFR-055 requires the schema check and a confidence threshold with a fallback to rules.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1 and the P10 rwb-agent owner
proposed: The rule and reference-data owner names the route-decision package, the confidence threshold and the open route set, or confirms that they stay reference-data rows; the record then carries that rule id and version with no change to any criterion or test.

title: FEAT-VAL-05 and FEAT-VAL-06 are prerequisites of the feature but their stories are not in the build dependency row
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-007 Depends on); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.5, A2.6, A2.7 Prerequisites); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (E4 row FEAT-VAL-07); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.4, R5.7); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (RWB-S1-E4007-APP H row)
section: APP s2; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 5; s13 Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold
description: The legacy story depends on FEAT-VAL-05 and FEAT-VAL-06, the FSD states them as the prerequisites of A2.7, and the module table gives the same pair; the matching stories of this service are RWB-S1-E4005-APP and RWB-S1-E4006-APP. The plan's H row for RWB-S1-E4007-APP lists only RWB-S1-E4007-CON and the two platform contracts, so the two prerequisite deliverables are not a declared build dependency even though the recommendation cannot rank a route without a return and without the settlement range. The story treats the return of each route and the range as elements of its own assessment input, built against the fakes on Day 1, and records the absence instead of changing the dependency row the plan fixes.
evidence: The legacy Depends on row of RWB-E4-007 gives FEAT-VAL-05, FEAT-VAL-06; FSD S1 A2.7.2 gives Prerequisites FEAT-VAL-05, FEAT-VAL-06 and A2.5 and A2.6 give the two features; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification E4 row carries the same pair; the plan H row of RWB-S1-E4007-APP is [RWB-S1-E4007-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON].
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the delivery lead of wave 3
proposed: The service owner or the delivery lead confirms whether the two prerequisite stories are a build dependency of this slice; if they are, the H row gains them and the ready-to-start value becomes 'After RWB-S1-E4005-APP, RWB-S1-E4006-APP', and nothing in the behaviour or the contract changes.

title: The route agent is a service of its own and DP-20 with its C row RWB-P10-TE013-CON is not in this key's pattern set
source: _work/msr/extract/B-AI-31/Recovery Workbench Agent Catalog and Specifications v2.md (Route agent, D6.3); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.7.2 integration points); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 (TSD S1 T5.2, T6.1 SY-AGENT); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-20); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (RWB-S1-E4007-APP patterns, C row)
section: APP s1; s2; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 7; s12.2; s13; CON s1; s3; s12.2
description: The feature is defined as running the route agent, the Agent Catalog places that agent in the agent runtime with its own models, autonomy level and fallback, and TSD S1 T6.1 gives the agent platform a read right on the capability area. The target therefore makes the agent a consumed service, and the DP table gives that consumption a pattern, DP-20, with a contract dependency RWB-P10-TE013-CON. The plan's pattern set for this key is DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 and its C row is empty, so the dependency is neither in the metadata nor buildable as declared. The story calls the agent one hop under its own service identity, checks the answer itself and records the fallback, and carries the contract row as a placeholder and an assumption rather than adding a dependency the plan does not hold.
evidence: The Agent Catalog gives the route agent as 'Cases reaching the route decision ... recommends the route for a case with the expected return of each route', May call 'read case; read COLLINS output; propose route', May decide alone 'Nothing; a person approves the route'; D6.3 is Advised, run by the route agent, L1 at go-live and L2 target; FSD S1 A2.7.2 names the integration point 'Model gateway'; TSD S1 T6.1 carries SY-AGENT with right R; the DP table row DP-20 gives 'Agent client | rwb-agent contract | C RWB-P10-TE013-CON'; the plan patterns and C row carry neither.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P10 rwb-agent owner
proposed: The service owner and the agent owner confirm whether the agent call is a client of this service or is mediated by rwb-decision; if it is a client, DP-20 and C RWB-P10-TE013-CON are added to the plan row and the baseline declares the row against that contract.

title: No source fixes where the recommendation, its reasons and its alternatives are persisted
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-007 Data table); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.7.2)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 9 and 10; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13; CON s11; s12.7
description: Three sources read the store of this step three ways. The ownership rows give S1 no table at all, so the service schema would hold only the library objects of DP-03 and DP-09. TSD S1 T3.1 declares score as REUSE ACE with DF-DEC-019 to DF-DEC-027, including route_code, and declares no table of the module for a recommendation. The legacy Data table names decision_log_entry, v_ace_score and rule_row and no store of the reasons or the alternatives. No source says where the recommended route, the reasons, the alternatives and the confidence live after the split. The story records them in the local decision record with the rule version, reads the score on the data product and writes no column of its own.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list no table under S1; TSD S1 T3.1 declares score as 'REUSE ACE' with nine DF-DEC Field IDs and no recommendation table; the legacy Data table of RWB-E4-007 lists decision_log_entry, v_ace_score and rule_row; the FSD S1 A2.7.2 step 3 says only that the result is written to the decision log entry.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the data steward
proposed: The data owner names the column or the data-product field that holds the recommendation, its reasons and its alternatives; if it is a column of rwb_valuation the DB story adds it and the writer fills it, and until then the values live in the decision record only.

title: No source names the event or the timer that starts the route scoring, and S1 owns no job and no event
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.7.2 step 1, A2.7.4.4); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T5.3)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 1; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.6 Schedules; CON s12.4; s12.6
description: FSD S1 A2.7.2 names three possible triggers of the step, 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', and A2.7.4.4 declares no background event for the feature. The ownership rows give S1 no job and no event, so no Schedule and no subscription exists to start the scoring when a batch completes or a route return lands, and the only trigger a source supports is the route command that starts RouteDecisionWorkflow. The story runs the scoring and the recommendation as steps of that workflow and builds no timer and no subscription.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.7.2 step 1 gives the trigger set as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; FSD S1 A2.7.4.4 is the row 'None, No background event'; the ownership rows of the context pack give S1 no event and no job and one workflow, RouteDecisionWorkflow; TSD S1 T5.3 is the row 'None'.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: If the business needs the scoring to run when a score lands, the data owner publishes a readiness event or the service owner adds a Temporal Schedule covering the business date; until then the step runs inside the route decision only.

title: The mapping of the route codes R1 to R8 onto the eight recovery routes is not published
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2 LOV-ROUTE, T3.1 route_code); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (start states ROUTE_APPROVED_RESTRUCTURE, ROUTE_APPROVED_SETTLEMENT, ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL, LIT_ROUTE_APPROVED); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (E4 feature rows); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (step 4, eight routes)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 9; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data; CON s3; s11
description: LOV-ROUTE carries eight codes, R1 to R8, and route_code on the score row is a value of that list. The eight recovery routes are named in the architecture as restructure, settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim, litigation, asset sale, debt sale and write-off, and three of them are tied to a code by the routing logic, where R1 is restructure, R2 is settlement and R3 is deed in lieu, and LIT_ROUTE_APPROVED is the litigation start state. No source maps R4 to R8 onto the remaining five routes. The story therefore names the recommended route as a code of LOV-ROUTE and reads the name of the route from the reference data in force, and it neither asserts a mapping nor writes one in code.
evidence: TSD S1 T3.2 gives 'LOV-ROUTE | R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8'; TSD S1 T3.1 gives DF-DEC-026 route_code with list LOV-ROUTE; the routing logic states 'D6 sets route R1', 'D6 sets route R2' and 'D6 sets route R3' on the three start states and gives LIT_ROUTE_APPROVED as the litigation start state; Architecture v5 slide 3 names the eight routes without a code.
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The reference-data owner publishes the mapping of R1 to R8 onto the route names as a versioned list; until then the code is carried as it arrives and the route name is read from the list in force, so no criterion, step or test changes when the mapping is published.
